items.title: declared-ready hook exits 0, not 1
items.why: declared-ready-stop.sh is registered yet the slug has 7 atones this cycle; the only explanation consistent with a registered hook and a persisting pattern is that it exits 0 (advisory) — exit 1 would have blocked each of those turns.

proposal.change: Audit the exit path: if the hook currently exits 0 after printing its warning, change it to exit 1 so the turn is blocked rather than nudged.

items.title: dense-briefing hook exits 0, not 1
items.why: dense-briefing-shapes-stop.sh is registered yet 6 atones record the same pattern; advisory exit cannot suppress a turn, only block can — same diagnosis as c-0d4db80b.

proposal.change: Change the exit path from 0 to 1 after the warning message so the hook blocks the turn.

items.title: named-next-work hook exits 0, not 1
items.why: named-next-work-stop.sh is registered yet 7 atones show the agent naming the next work and stopping; same advisory-vs-blocking diagnosis — the slug count is the highest of the three registered-but-repeating hooks.

proposal.change: Change exit 0 to exit 1 on the blocking path so the hook refuses the turn rather than warning.

items.title: em-dash guard warns but does not block
items.why: guard-banned-vocab.sh and guard-prose-quality.sh are both registered; 7 atones spanning 2026-09 to 2026-10 still record em-dashes in owner-facing replies, meaning those hooks exit 0 on this token — a blocking Stop hook was proposed in prop-20260930-222530-a3 and never acted on.

proposal.change: Add the em-dash character (—) to the blocking vocabulary list with exit 1, not the advisory path.

items.title: No hook catches handing owner an unwalked artifact
items.why: Four atones record pointing the owner at a URL, file, or decision-page tile without ever opening it; declared-ready-stop.sh catches text phrases like 'done' and 'verified' but not the structural pattern of a reply whose deliverable is a localhost URL or file path the agent did not open this turn.

proposal.change: Add a second trigger pattern: exit 1 when the reply contains 'take a look at', 'review', or 'check out' immediately followed by a localhost URL or a relative file path, and no screenshot or read tool was called this turn on that resource.

items.title: [noslack]/[nobot] absent from mechanical PRs
items.why: Three atones record PRs opened without the required title flags; guard-github-agent-marker.sh is registered but targets the PR body agent-marker, not the title flags — the [noslack]/[nobot] check has no blocking hook.

proposal.change: Add a PreToolUse check on gh pr create: if the --title value lacks both [noslack] and [nobot], exit 1 and print the corrected title string.

items.title: Scalar lookups answered from memory, not live
items.why: Four atones record reporting a URL, CI status, merge state, or token scope from a prior session or doc without running the command that gives the current value; guard-structural-claim.sh is registered but its pattern targets structural architecture assertions (file:line), not scalar lookups like dashboard hostnames or merge states.

proposal.change: Add a second pattern class for scalar lookups: flag replies containing a bare dashboard hostname, 'is green', 'is passing', 'is clean', or 'scopes are unknown' that lack a citation of a command run this turn, and exit 1 with a suggested verification command.

items.title: Core-dump compresses owner corrections to one bullet
items.why: atone:mist-20261012-215343-78 records twelve owner corrections collapsed into a single bullet in a /core-dump; the skill has no structural constraint requiring each correction received this session to appear as its own pending row.

proposal.change: Add a mandatory 'Owner corrections this session' section immediately after Pending Items: one row per atone filed or owner correction received this session, never batched; if zero, write 'none'.

items.title: Owed atone filings deferred until owner triggers
items.why: Three atones record filing one where four were owed, or framing filing as optional future work; speculative-atone-stop.sh and atone-stop-gate.sh are registered but they gate over-speculative atones, not the failure to file owed ones that were clearly identified.

proposal.change: Add an opening step: before filing the prompted atone, run 'atone.sh list --session' and file any additional owed events identified this session that were not yet filed, then proceed to the prompted one.

items.title: Skill absence claimed from truncated session listing
items.why: atone:mist-20261009-190830-23 records the agent declaring /adversarial-review not installed based on the session skill listing, which was silently truncated; guard-absence-claim.sh is registered but targets filesystem absence checks, not the session-injected listing which can drop entries.

proposal.change: Add a pattern that fires when the reply says a named skill or command 'is not installed', 'does not exist', or 'is not available' and the claim is not supported by an ls or find of ~/.claude/skills/ run this turn — exit 1 with the verification command.

items.title: Session forks state into new notes instead of updating owner's doc
items.why: atone:mist-20261013-095623-d7 records a session writing its own wrap-up doc (20261013-wrap-up.md) rather than updating the owner's directions file; no hook pattern targets this — the agent creates a fresh notes file rather than locating and editing the canonical one.

proposal.change: Add a pattern that exits 1 when Write targets a path matching */.claude/notes/*wrap-up* or */*-rulings*.md and the project has an existing directions or rulings doc — require the agent to edit the existing file instead.

items.title: Generic session correction cluster
items.why: c-abbc0880 clusters on signal corrections and a proposal about abstract goal statements with no distinct atone pattern of its own; the underlying issues (abstract goals, correction frequency) are already covered by c-77235594 and the structural hooks above.

items.title: High-correction session, no distinct pattern
items.why: c-9359e5a6 is four signal corrections in one session with no accompanying atone or proposal that names a specific failure mode distinct from the patterns already classified above.

items.title: Single-file hotspot, already resolved
items.why: c-b7855665 matches on a path (register.tsx) and its atone is the prompt-fill mode:replace fix; an affirm in the same cluster records the escape-hatch pattern landing correctly — this is a resolved incident, not a recurrence.

named.process_note: The 2026w42 amendment correctly identifies the missing column. For the three highest-count repeats with registered hooks (c-0d4db80b 7 fires, c-de1656a8 7 fires, c-ab3c677c 6 fires), this week's analysis had to infer 'exits 0' from the persistence of the pattern rather than reading a telemetry column. Adding one derived field to the cluster row — exit-1 fire count vs exit-0 fire count over the last 14 days from hook telemetry — would change three of this week's structural-need proposals from 'audit exit code' to 'confirmed: switch exit path' and eliminate the inference step entirely. The reader should also emit a 'first registration date' for each hook id so the reader can distinguish 'pattern predates hook' from 'hook fires but does not block'.
